''Coprosma baueri'' auct. non Endl.
''Coprosma retusa'' Hook. f
''Coprosma stockii'' Williams | status = NT | status_system = NZTCS | status_ref = {{Cite web |title=NZTCS |url=https://nztcs.org.nz/assessments/113093 |access-date=2025-03-03 |website=nztcs.org.nz}} }} '''''Coprosma repens''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant|flowering]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] of the [[genus]] ''[[Coprosma]]'', in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Rubiaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to New Zealand.{{cite web|url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/|title=WCSP |work= World Checklist of Selected Plant Families|access-date=8 June 2019}} Common names include '''taupata''', '''tree bedstraw''',{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }} '''mirror bush''', '''looking-glass bush''', '''New Zealand laurel''' and '''shiny leaf'''.{{cite web|title=Weed Identification - Looking glass bush|publisher=Australian Weeds Committee|work=Weeds Australia|url=http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&ibra=all&card=E30|access-date=2012-08-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120420005340/http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&ibra=all&card=E30|archive-date=2012-04-20|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Coprosma~repens |title=Coprosma repens A.Rich.|access-date=2009-04-26 |work= PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia}}{{cite web|title=Shiny Leaf - ''Coprosma repens''|work=Environmental Weeds of the South East|publisher=Department of Environment and Heritage South Australia|url=http://www.senrm.sa.gov.au/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=DsN9pDdJ24k%3D&tabid=1706&mid=2683|access-date=2009-04-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090523124016/http://www.senrm.sa.gov.au/LinkClick.aspx?fileticket=DsN9pDdJ24k%3d&tabid=1706&mid=2683|archive-date=2009-05-23|url-status=dead}} ==Description== The habit of this species varies markedly with its situation. In exposed situations, such as cliffs, it assumes a [[Prostrate shrub|prostrate habit]], while in more sheltered areas it can grow as a small tree up to 8 metres in height.{{cite web |url=http://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/pages/Taxon.aspx?id=_3f21850b-8f3f-4723-ae60-56cbb420ec3a&fileName=Flora%201.xml#_3f21850b-8f3f-4723-ae60-56cbb420ec3a |title=''Coprosma repens''|work=Flora of New Zealand Series|publisher=Landcare Research|access-date=2009-04-26}} It has thick and very glossy leaves which vary considerably in size, depending on exposure to the elements. The leaf margins are recurved, occasionally to the extent that the leaf may be cylindrical in cross-section. The shiny leaves aid its survival near coastal locations. ''C. repens'' is [[dioecy|dioecious]]. Flowers are produced in spring and summer, with the male flowers appearing in dense, compound clusters, and the female flowers in smaller clusters. Male flowers have a funnel shaped [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] that is 5 mm long, with lobes equal to the tube. Female flowers have a short [[calyx (botany)|calyx]], and a tubular corolla 3 mm long, with lobes shorter than the tube. Female plants produce orange-red ovoid [[drupe]]s, which are about 8 mm in diameter and 10 mm in length. ==Distribution== The species is native to the [[North Island]], [[South Island]], [[Kermadec Islands]] and [[Three Kings Islands]] in New Zealand. In Australia, it has become [[naturalization (biology)|naturalised]] in coastal areas of Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania, and it is now classified as an environmental [[weed]]. ==Cultivation== {{multiple image | align = right | footer = Taupata flowers | width1 = 105 | image1 = Male_taupata_flower_(Coprosma_repens).jpg | alt1 = Cluster of cream-coloured anthers on droopy white stalks | caption1 = Male | width2 = 110 | image2 = Female_taupata_flower_(Coprosma_repens).jpg | alt2 = Cluster of translucent purple stalks, curving upward | caption2 = Female }} The species has been popular in coastal gardens due to its resistance to salt spray. Although it prefers well-drained sandy soils, it can cope with heavier soils. There is a large number of [[cultivar]]s: *'Coffee Cream' - creamy yellow leaf margins *'Coppershine' - foliage with a copper-bronze tinge *'Evening Glow' - golden foliage which changes to rich orange and pink-red shades during autumn and winter[http://plantselector.botanicgardens.sa.gov.au/Plants/Details/52 Coprosma repens 'Evening Glow'] *'Marble Chips' - leaves with white margins and speckles *'Picturata' - leaves with a golden central area *'Pink Splendour' - leaves have pink and maroon shaded margins *'Rainbow Surprise' - a small cultivar with small pink and yellow-green leaves *'Taupata Gold' - cream leaves with green centres *'Variegata' - leaves with a creamy-white margin *'Yvonne' - compact form with dark-green leaves{{cite book|author= Kirsten, Keith|author2 = Lizelle Meyer-Faedda | title= Gardening with Keith Kirsten |publisher=Struik Press| year=2001 | isbn=1868725073|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B1sqtRz50ToC&q=Coprosma+repens+cultivars&pg=PA92}} {{Dead link|date=February 2022}} The cultivars 'Marble Queen'{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector -
